scope: Texas health access and cross-domain planning. These are operational facts/program descriptions, not individualized medical advice or guaranteed eligibility.

facts.statement: Texas HHSC states routine nonemergency medical transportation requests should generally be made at least two workdays before an appointment, or five days before an appointment outside the county; specified same-day situations may qualify.
facts.limitations: Program eligibility and scheduling details must be verified for the individual and health plan.

facts.statement: Texas HHSC lists public transportation, taxi/van service, and commercial transit among possible NEMT ride types, and describes gas assistance and some lodging/meal support under program rules.
facts.limitations: Not all options apply to every beneficiary or trip.

facts.statement: Texas DSHS and HRSA use HPSA and MUA/P designations to identify shortages and target certain workforce and access programs.
facts.limitations: Designation does not measure every dimension of real-world appointment access.

facts.statement: Texas DSHS requires certification for CHWs/promotores who are compensated for CHW services; DSHS describes training- and experience-based certification pathways.
facts.limitations: Verify current application and renewal requirements directly with DSHS.

facts.statement: Updated Texas CHW core competencies became effective February 1, 2026, and DSHS required training-center curricula to align by August 1, 2026.
facts.limitations: Training-center implementation and course availability can change.

facts.statement: Texas's BEAD Final Proposal was approved December 4, 2025. The Broadband Development Office reports 22 selected applicants, more than 240,000 broadband-serviceable locations, more than 2,700 community anchor institutions, $1.2 billion in federal grant funds and $177 million in state match.
facts.limitations: Awards and approved locations do not prove that service is already constructed, activated, affordable or adequate for a specific telehealth use.

facts.statement: Texas HHSC's SFY 2026 Pediatric Tele-Connectivity Resource Program for Rural Texas was designed to connect rural hospitals and rural health clinics with pediatric specialists/subspecialists or eligible higher-education partners in the Texas Child Mental Health Care Consortium.
facts.limitations: The RFA is a program record; current award and operational status should be verified separately.

facts.statement: CMS's 2026 hospital price-transparency requirements added median, 10th-percentile and 90th-percentile allowed amounts plus counts for certain percentage/algorithm-based negotiated charges, with enforcement of new/revised 2026 requirements beginning April 1, 2026.
facts.limitations: Published standard charges are not a guaranteed patient bill and may not capture all individual coverage details.

facts.statement: Texas HHSC points people to 988, Texas 2-1-1 and 24/7 Local Mental Health/Behavioral Health Authority crisis lines for behavioral-health crisis navigation.
facts.limitations: Immediate threats to life or safety require emergency services.

facts.statement: Texas DSHS Health Data publishes maternal-health dashboards covering maternal mortality, pregnancy planning, maternal mental health and physical-health factors, with documented source and methodology notes.
facts.limitations: Dashboard years and indicator availability vary; use the displayed data vintage for analysis.

facts.statement: TCEQ maintains separate official Texas air-quality and public drinking-water information systems that can be used as environmental context layers in community health planning.
facts.limitations: Environmental measurements do not establish an individual's medical diagnosis.

facts.statement: Trystero documents TURN as a relay fallback when direct WebRTC peer connections cannot be established under some network conditions; configured TURN traffic remains part of the WebRTC encrypted transport path.
facts.limitations: TURN requires an operator/service and credentials/configuration; this bundle does not ship hidden TURN infrastructure.

facts.statement: HRSA states that Health Center Program clinics provide primary medical and dental care to people whether or not they have insurance and adjust fees using a sliding scale based on ability to pay.
facts.limitations: Services, hours, capacity and appointment availability vary by clinic and must be verified.

facts.statement: Texas HHSC provides a county/ZIP service finder for AAA, ADRC, LMHA and LIDDA offices and lists 855-937-2372 for help identifying services.
facts.limitations: Office coverage and contact details can change; verify the live directory.

facts.statement: Texas HHSC lists the Texas Medicare Help Line at 800-252-9240 and HICAP as a source of free Medicare benefits counseling.
facts.limitations: Counseling supports navigation; it does not make plan decisions for users.

facts.statement: CMS says a federal patient-provider dispute process may be available for eligible uninsured/self-pay bills that are at least $400 above a good-faith estimate, subject to program rules and exceptions.
facts.limitations: Not all services/plans are covered by the same protections; ground ambulance bills are an important federal exception.

facts.statement: Texas HHS describes Early Childhood Intervention as serving children from birth up to 36 months with qualifying developmental delay, disability or certain diagnosed conditions.
facts.limitations: The OS does not assess developmental eligibility or diagnose a child.
